description: This course covers the fundamentals of information storage and retrieval, including data modeling using relational and NoSQL databases; search algorithms such as inverted indexes and Boolean retrieval; information retrieval models like the Vector Space Model and BM25; text preprocessing techniques including tokenization, stemming, and stopword removal; indexing strategies for large-scale data; query processing and optimization techniques; and evaluation metrics such as precision, recall, and F1-score. The course also explores distributed systems for data storage, including technologies like Hadoop and Apache Cassandra; cloud-based storage solutions such as Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage; and standards such as ACID properties and SQL/NoSQL query languages. Additional topics include information retrieval in web search engines, recommendation systems using collaborative filtering and matrix factorization, and the ethical considerations of data storage and retrieval.

clos.text: Define relational and NoSQL database models, including their schema design, ACID properties, and query languages such as SQL and MongoDB.
Describe the inverted index data structure and its role in efficient text retrieval, along with Boolean and vector space retrieval models.
Explain the principles of text preprocessing, including tokenization, stemming, stopword removal, and lemmatization, and their impact on search quality.
Apply indexing strategies and query optimization techniques to improve the performance of information retrieval systems using technologies like Elasticsearch and Apache Solr.
Evaluate the effectiveness of information retrieval systems using metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (MAP).

topics: Introduction to Information Storage and Retrieval
Data Models: Relational vs. NoSQL Databases
Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage
Information Retrieval in Web Search Engines
Elasticsearch and Apache Solr for Search Applications
Ethical and Legal Aspects of Data Storage
